newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lufthansa warns new HK airport over landing fees.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa warns new HK airport over landing fees.

text.p: A member of the executive board of Lufthansa Cargo AG, Stefan Lauer, has voiced his concern over proposed landing fees as Hong Kong's new airport.

After losses of 60 million marks last year, Lauer said cost control was vital to the airline's future and it would be 104 percent more expensive to operate from the new Chek Lap Kok compared to Hong Kong's existing Kai Tak.

If Lufthansa switched operations to the new, but so far under developed airport at nearby Macau, it would save two million marks a year or around HK$10 million from the cost of operating from Kai Tak.
Lauer stressed that Lufthansa Cargo has no plans to relocate to an alternative airport in the Pearl River delta but other cargo carriers may be tempted.

"We are concerned about the widening cost gap that already exists and we all know there are alternatives (airports). ....I really expect some of the low profile, low cost carriers to explore the opportunities and make a test. If it is a success, others will follow. Only if costs remain at a reasonable level and quality high will Hong Kong keep its prominent position" Lauer told reporters.

The latest warning is part of a continuing campaign by the airlines to try and force Hong Kong's Airport Authority to rethink its pricing policy at Chek Lap Kok. Lauer said his chief operating officer had already lobbied the Authority via the international Air Transport Association (IATA).
